top_choice_rationale: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a general, mechanistically understood, ligand-controlled method that has been independently reproduced for three decades and is routine in pharmaceutical and process chemistry. Buchwald and Hartwig independently made it general by removing the stoichiometric tin amide of the Migita/Kosugi reaction, so a two-name citation built on the word general is clean. The 2010 overlap is real but the elementary-step bottleneck (amine binding, deprotonation, C-N reductive elimination) and the ligand problem differ from C-C coupling. P002 is a new design principle but has no approved degrader and an unresolved PROTAC versus cereblon glue credit split, so it ranks second, above no award.
